questions.question: Which living organism is considered the largest by volume?
questions.hint: General Sherman, a Giant Sequoia in California, is the largest known single-stem tree by volume.

questions.question: Which bird is capable of flying at the highest recorded altitude?
questions.hint: A Rüppell's Griffon Vulture has been recorded flying at approximately 11,300 meters (37,100 feet).

questions.question: Which film franchise features the fictional artifact known as the "One Ring"?
questions.hint: The One Ring is the central object in J.R.R. Tolkien's epic fantasy saga.

questions.question: Which animated film became the first to win the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature?
questions.hint: Shrek won the inaugural Best Animated Feature Oscar in 2002.

questions.question: Which organization publishes the annual World Happiness Report?
options: United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)
questions.hint: The report is produced by the SDSN with support from the United Nations.

questions.question: Which international organization is responsible for protecting cultural property during armed conflict through the Hague Convention?
questions.hint: UNESCO oversees international efforts to safeguard cultural heritage during times of war.

questions.question: Which emperor commissioned the construction of the Terracotta Army?
questions.hint: China's first emperor ordered the creation of thousands of life-sized terracotta soldiers to guard his tomb.

questions.question: Which famous naval battle in 1805 secured British naval dominance during the Napoleonic Wars?
questions.hint: Admiral Horatio Nelson's victory at Trafalgar ensured British naval supremacy for more than a century.

questions.question: Which athlete has won the most Olympic medals in history?
questions.hint: Michael Phelps has won 28 Olympic medals, including 23 gold medals, more than any athlete in history.

questions.question: Which nation won the inaugural FIFA Women's World Cup in 1991?
questions.hint: The United States defeated Norway to become the first FIFA Women's World Cup champions.

questions.question: Which country has the greatest number of active volcanoes?
questions.hint: Indonesia sits along the Pacific Ring of Fire and has more active volcanoes than any other country.

questions.question: Which lake is the deepest in the world?
questions.hint: Lake Baikal in Siberia reaches a depth of 1,642 meters (5,387 feet) and contains about 20% of the world's unfrozen surface freshwater.

questions.question: Which scientist proposed the uncertainty principle?
questions.hint: The uncertainty principle states that certain pairs of physical properties cannot both be known with perfect precision simultaneously.

questions.question: Which particle is responsible for carrying the electromagnetic force?
questions.hint: Photons are the force carrier particles (gauge bosons) of electromagnetism.

questions.question: Which civilization created the Nazca Lines?
questions.hint: The Nazca people created enormous geoglyphs in southern Peru between about 500 BC and AD 500.

questions.question: Which language is written using the Devanagari script?
questions.hint: Hindi is primarily written in the Devanagari script, one of the world's oldest continuously used writing systems.

questions.question: Which marine animal is known to have three hearts?
questions.hint: An octopus has three hearts—two pump blood to the gills, while one pumps blood to the rest of the body.

questions.question: Which country contains the largest number of UNESCO World Heritage Sites?
questions.hint: Italy has long ranked among the countries with the highest number of UNESCO World Heritage Sites, reflecting its rich cultural and historical heritage.

questions.question: Which scientist developed the periodic table of elements?
questions.hint: Dmitri Mendeleev organized the elements by recurring chemical properties and accurately predicted several undiscovered elements. Although he did not receive a Nobel Prize, he is widely credited with creating the modern periodic table.

questions.question: Which treaty divided newly discovered lands outside Europe between Spain and Portugal in 1494?
questions.hint: The Treaty of Tordesillas established a demarcation line giving Spain and Portugal separate spheres of exploration and colonization.
